 Tamil music maestro Ilaiyaraaja to Malaysian fans: Thanks for keeping it quiet, and see you at Bukit Jalil Feb 2027 
 Copy 
 Legendary South Indian music composer Ilaiyaraaja is scheduled to perform at Stadium Nasional Bukit Jalil in Kuala Lumpur on February 6, 2027. — Picture from Instagram/ilaiyaraaja_offl

 Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 7:40 PM MYT 
 KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Legendary South Indian music composer Ilaiyaraaja says Malaysian fans hold a special place in his heart, describing their disciplined and deeply appreciative nature as something he has come to cherish over the years. 
 He said he was particularly touched by how Malaysian audiences quietly appreciated his music during concerts, and expressed their excitement and joy through social media afterwards.
 “Every time I perform in Malaysia, I realise how much the fans appreciate my music. 
 “They listen attentively to each song during the concert, and afterwards, I see them sharing their happiness and excitement. 
 “What I particularly appreciate is their discipline. 
 “They listen so attentively, without excessive whistling or shouting.
 “That is something special about Malaysian audiences,” he said in his speech at an event to announce RAAJA 50, a concert celebrating his 50-year journey in the Indian film industry, at the TSR Conference Hall, IRDKL Mall in Shah Alam, Selangor, yesterday.
 The concert, organised by PINK ASIA and MERCURI, is scheduled to take place at Stadium Nasional Bukit Jalil here on February 6, 2027.
 RAAJA 50 will feature a 70-piece live orchestra comprising musicians from Europe and India, performing the composer’s celebrated works.
 The event will also bring together prominent personalities from South Indian cinema, including filmmakers, actors and singers, to honour the musical maestro whose compositions have influenced generations.
 The 1976 Tamil film Annakkili marked Ilaiyaraaja’s debut as a music director.
 He introduced a distinctive musical style that blended traditional Indian melodies with Western classical harmonies and orchestration.
 Over the last five decades, he has composed music for more than 1,500 films and produced over 8,600 songs, establishing himself as one of the most prolific composers in Indian cinema.
 In March 2025, his Symphony No. 1 — Valiant premiered in London, with the Royal Philharmonic Concert Orchestra performing the composition, marking another milestone in his musical career.
 Ticket sales for RAAJA 50 will be announced soon, with prices starting from RM99. — Bernama
